title: Tenant-aware ingress shaper with soft-deadlines and kernel residency to reduce embedding p99
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: embedding endpoint p99 spikes under bursting tenant traffic and heterogeneous request sizes. Root causes identified in prior profiling: (1) small-batch storming that prevents efficient kernel coalescing, (2) cold kernel/resident state thrash when quantized kernels are loaded on demand, and (3) lack of per-tenant soft deadlines causing high-priority requests to be delayed behind large background batches.

Objective: Implement a tenant-aware ingress shaper that assigns per-tenant soft-deadlines (soft-SLOs) and maintains a small kernel residency pool for hot kernels to reduce load-time kernel swap and tail latency. Combine this with an adaptive micro-batching window that respects soft-deadlines and triggers speculative kernel selection when a deadline is close. Goal: reduce embedding endpoint p99 from baseline (~420ms) to <=260ms at expected 95th-percentile load while keeping p50 within 5% of baseline and no >5% increase in token cost.

Scope: implementation spans routing/ingress, scheduler (batching window), kernel manager (residency pool + prewarm hooks), and monitoring/alerting. Includes canary rollout with per-tenant flags and circuit-breaker rollback.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embedding /v1/embeddings under standard benchmark workload reduced to <=260ms measured over 24h canary at 80% traffic
no more than 5% regression in p50 and overall token cost compared to baseline
per-tenant soft-deadline config exposed in Console and API; defaults documented
kernel residency maintains >90% hit rate for top-10 kernels on a canary fleet
automated rollback if error-rate or p99 increases by >15% during canary
notes: Design trade-offs: short aggregation windows reduce latency but lower batching efficiency; we will use soft-deadlines to select between low-latency and high-throughput paths per-request.
Kernel residency: limited pool of preloaded quantized/native kernels kept per-GPU instance; size tuned to keep memory overhead <6% of GPU memory on average.
Speculative kernel selection: when a request is within 15ms of its soft-deadline, scheduler may route to a lower-precision but warm kernel to avoid tail blowups.
Tenant-awareness: tenants can opt into strict-low-latency mode (higher cost) or best-effort batching; default is best-effort with soft-deadlines enabled.
Security: no sensitive customer data moves into residency pool; residency only caches kernel code and quant tables, not KV cache or request payloads.
